content: The Court of Genova resolved a complex division involving a two-unit building where shares were split 1/3 and 2/3. The judge analyzed the "convenient divisibility" not just structurally, but in relation to the legal shares. It was found that assigning one of the units would force the 1/3 shareholder to pay an excessive cash settlement. Because the resulting lots did not match the ownership percentages, the division in nature was declared impossible. The court then addressed the husband's liability for "occupational indemnity" regarding the common units. It was determined that the husband had leased one unit to his son at an abnormally low price without consent. The judge ordered the husband to pay the wife 1/3 of the actual market rental value. This reimbursement started from the date of the legal claim for the units no longer assigned to him.
